claim: Let \(A=\{a_0,a_1,a_2\}\subset\mathbb Z\) have three distinct points, put \(g=\gcd(a_1-a_0,a_2-a_0)>0\), \(u=(a_1-a_0)/g\), and \(v=(a_2-a_0)/g\). Then \(A\) is spectral if and only if it tiles \(\mathbb Z\), and this happens exactly when \(\{u\bmod 3,v\bmod 3\}=\{1,2\}\). In that case every normalized spectrum \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) with \(0\in\Gamma\) is uniquely of the form \(\Gamma_{r,s}=\{0,(3r+1)/(3g),(3s+2)/(3g)\}\) for \(0\le r,s<g\), so there are exactly \(g^2\) normalized spectra. Moreover every translational tiling complement is uniquely \(T=-a_0+\bigcup_{r=0}^{g-1}(r+g(c_r+3\mathbb Z))\) with \(c_r\in\{0,1,2\}\), so there are exactly \(3^g\) complements; in particular every complement is \(3g\)-periodic.
integrity: The theorem is proved from explicit unit-circle, finite-state periodicity, and finite Fourier arguments. Finite exhaustive checks are used only as sanity checks and are not substituted for the proof.
scientific_limitations: The proof is restricted to three-point subsets of the integers. The accessible literature comparison did not include the full text of arXiv:2607.19858, so an equivalent low-cardinality parametrization under different notation remains a residual literature risk.
title: Complete spectral and tiling moduli for three-point integer sets
